1.title: Remembered
1.description:
The Abyssal Guardian kneels in the dust. Before its light goes out, it studies your face, and something like recognition crosses its own.

'Not yet,' it rasps. 'But soon.'

variants.title: Again
variants.description:
The Abyssal Guardian kneels in the dust. 'Again,' it rasps, almost fondly. 'You always open with the left.'

You don't. You never have. You check your stance.

You did.

2.title: Worn Steps
2.description:
The Vile Serpent coils and goes still. You look down at the staircase. Every step is hollowed in the middle, polished by countless boots.

But only going up. Not one step is worn on the way down.

Nobody has ever walked back out of here.

3.title: The Whispers
3.description:
Grakthar falls, and the chamber goes quiet enough to hear the whispers clearly. They're counting: floors, steps, days.

One voice near the ceiling keeps repeating a single phrase: 'Don't give it the summit.'

You don't know what it means. You remember it anyway.

variants.description:
Grakthar falls, and the chamber goes quiet enough to hear the whispers clearly. They're counting: floors, steps, days.

One voice near the ceiling keeps repeating a single phrase: 'Don't give it the summit.'

It's your voice.

4.title: Tithe
4.description:
Voss crumbles. Beneath his throne of bones sits an offering bowl, still warm, glowing faintly with strength drawn from the fallen.

Carved around its rim are three sigils: a sun, a skull and a broken spiral.

Elysia. Sepulchure. Drakath. All three drink from the same bowl.

5.title: The Toll
5.description:
The Marauder falls, laughing. 'You were going to say this morning, weren't you? Everyone says this morning.'

He presses a stolen pocket watch into your hand. It still ticks. The date on its little dial is years later than the one you remember.

6.title: The Thread
6.description:
The Queen dies in her web. Every strand hums, and one is warm to the touch. Yours.

You follow it upward with your eyes, through the ceiling, toward the summit. Near the top it doesn't end. It bends back down and ties itself to the foot of the Tower.

A circle.

7.title: The Count
7.description:
Moros fades. Where he stood lies a bone charm on an old cord, scored with a hundred tiny notches.

On the back, freshly cut, is a single mark that wasn't there a moment ago.

You take it. Somehow you know you'll need something to count on.

variants.description:
Moros fades. Something in your pack is suddenly heavy: a bone charm you don't remember owning, scored with notches.

You count them. {PREV_CYCLE}.

Your hand moves before you can think, and cuts one more. {CYCLE}. It feels like a habit.

8.title: Fuel
8.description:
The Behemoth's furnace gutters out. Inside its chest, instead of coal, are hundreds of glass beads. Each holds a tiny frozen scene: a farewell, a first sword, a birthday.

Memories. The Tower burns them for heat.

One bead rolls against your boot. You don't look at it. You're afraid it's yours.

9.title: Painted Window
9.description:
The Matriarch's wings shatter into prisms. Past the gate is a window, the first you've seen in the Tower, showing a green valley and a road home.

You reach for it. Your fingers meet cold stone. The window is painted on.

Scratched beneath it, in a dozen different hands: 'IT ONLY GOES UP.'

10.title: A Knock
10.description:
The mirror shatters. For a heartbeat every shard shows a different door, and behind one of them, not a god's door, just a plain wooden one, something knocks back.

Once. Like an answer.

11.title: Tally Marks
11.description:
The Sanctum walls are covered floor to ceiling in tally marks, cut by thousands of hands. By the far door, in fresh chalk, is a little drawing of a bird and a line of neat writing:

'If you can read this, you still remember how to read. Good. Keep climbing. Find me on 13. -W'

12.title: Livestock
12.description:
Kael laughs as he fades. 'Chosen. Sponsored. Champion. Such pretty words for a crop.'

You look at your hands, calloused and stronger than yesterday. Every floor has made you more.

More to take.

13.title: The Plan
13.description:
Ignis Inferno gutters out. Wren sits on the cooling rock, chalk dust on her fingers.

'Listen, because you'll forget. Three keys are hidden above: Floors 22, 23 and 25. The Tower fights to keep them. Carry all three to the top and there's a fourth door. Not a god's door. Ours.'

The floor begins to reset around her. 'Go. Hold it open for me.'

14.title: A Warning

god_messages.elysia:
*A voice like dawn, heavy with shame:*
"I told myself this was mercy. Purpose for mortals who had none. When you reach the top, do not stop at my door." - **Elysia**
god_messages.sepulchure:
*A voice like a closing tomb:*
"I won't pretend to care for you. But I despise waste, and this tower wastes champions. Keep climbing. Surprise me." - **Sepulchure**
god_messages.drakath:
*A voice that laughs in three directions at once:*
"Rules are only walls you haven't kicked yet. There are more doors at the top than we admit. Count them." - **Drakath**

15.title: Left Behind
15.description:
Behind Infernus's throne is an armory of things climbers left behind: swords, lockets, letters never sent. Every item hangs from a hook with a name tag.

One empty hook has a fresh tag. The ink is still wet.

It's your name.

variants.description:
Behind Infernus's throne is an armory of things climbers left behind: swords, lockets, letters never sent. Every item hangs from a hook with a name tag.

One tag reads {PLAYER}. Tied to it is a letter in your own handwriting. It says only:

'Get the keys. Trust Wren.'

16.title: Borrowed Faces
16.description:
The Shapeshifter comes apart like wet paper, and the stolen faces drift free, blinking and confused.

They were never illusions. The Tower copies every climber it can reach and keeps the copies on a shelf.

Somewhere out there, {minion1_name} and {minion2_name} just felt a chill and couldn't say why.

17.title: What's Left
17.description:
The Devourer bursts, and everything it swallowed spills across the floor: refusals, apologies, a thousand unfinished no's.

One of them drifts into you and settles behind your ribs.

For the first time since you entered, you feel like you could say no to a god.

18.title: Eleven Hundred and One
18.description:
Chromaggus crashes through his own roost and lies still. The Blood Warden kneels over him, not in grief but in bookkeeping.

'He'll be back,' it tells you, unbothered. 'Nothing in the Tower goes to waste. Not him. Not you.'

19.title: Stand Still
19.description:
The Overlord dissipates, but the Spiral keeps turning, stairs sliding past like a river. Walking only brings you back.

So you stand still. You close your eyes and count to a hundred.

When you open them, the stairs have carried you to the exit. The Tower yields to whoever stops playing its game.

20.title: The Frozen
20.description:
Frostbite shatters. In the ice behind him, preserved like pressed flowers, stand dozens of climbers frozen mid-step. They look peaceful.

One of them has a hand pressed flat against the ice from the inside, pointing up.

Far above, you hear it again: a knock on a plain wooden door.

21.title: Recycled
21.description:
Chromaggus falls a second time, in exactly the same way, with exactly the same roar. Far below, stone grinds as the Tower starts building him again.

This is what it wants from you too. Not your death.

Your repetition.

22.title: The First Key
22.description: Shriekara's last scream splits her throne in two.

variants.description:
Shriekara's last scream splits her throne in two. From the wreckage rises a key of pale bone, singing one clear note.

It drops into your palm, cold as winter.

variants.title: Taken
variants.description:
Shriekara's last scream splits her throne in two. A key of pale bone rises from the wreckage, singing one clear note, and the floor opens like a mouth and swallows it.

The Tower has taken it back. This cycle.
Shriekara's last scream splits her throne in two. In your pack, the bone key hums in answer. It's already yours.

23.title: The Second Key
23.description: Malgros collapses into a pool of starless dark.

variants.description:
Malgros collapses into a pool of starless dark. Floating on its surface is a key of black glass that reflects nothing, not even you.

You lift it out. The dark ripples, almost grateful.

variants.title: Sunk
variants.description:
Malgros collapses into a pool of starless dark. A key of black glass floats on its surface for one breath, then sinks, and the pool seals over like ice.

The Tower keeps what it can.
Malgros collapses into a pool of starless dark. The glass key in your pack grows cold, as if in mourning.

24.title: The Heart
24.description:
Vorath falls, and at last you see the Tower's heart: a vast chamber of glowing threads, one for every climber, all drawn up into the dark.

Yours is there. So is Wren's, knotted tight around Floor 13. So are thousands more.

The heart beats once. The whole Tower breathes in.

25.title: The Third Key
25.description: The Overfiend smiles as he cools to stone.

variants.description:
The Overfiend smiles as he cools to stone. In his cracked chest glows a key of red-hot iron. It doesn't burn you. It fits your hand as if it were made for it.

Perhaps it was.

variants.title: Next Time
variants.description:
The Overfiend smiles as he cools to stone. In his cracked chest glows a key of red-hot iron, until the Tower reaches in with a hundred stone fingers and drags it into the walls.

His smile doesn't fade. 'Next time,' whisper his ashes.
The Overfiend smiles as he cools to stone. The iron key in your pack glows warm, keeping his fire.

26.title: Keep It
26.description:
Malroth falls, and for a moment he looks almost relieved.

'Keep it,' he says. 'Whatever they offer you up there, keep the part of you that stops for strangers. The gods can't drink that.'

variants.description:
Malroth falls, and for a moment he looks almost relieved.

'You were kinder, the cycle we climbed together,' he says. 'You still are, a little. Keep that. The gods can't drink it.'

27.title: Chalk
27.description:
The Leviathan sinks into black water. On the wall above the stairs is a little chalk bird, and beneath it:

'I heard you pass 13. I always hear. Whatever door you choose, choose it for you, not for me. -W'

The chalk is still soft. She drew it on a floor she can never reach. Somehow.

28.title: The Ledger
28.description:
Enderark settles like a closing book. Beneath it lies the Tower's ledger: every climber, every summit, every choice.

Elysia's door. Sepulchure's door. Drakath's door. Page after page after page.

The last column has no header. Every line of it is empty. Waiting.

29.title: The Last Stair
29.description:
Abaddon's tide drains away, revealing the final staircase, lit gold from above.

Your pack holds no keys this cycle. You climb anyway.

variants.description:
Abaddon's tide drains away, revealing the final staircase, lit gold from above.

{KEYS} of three keys clink together in your pack. Not a full set. You climb anyway.

Abaddon's tide drains away, revealing the final staircase, lit gold from above.

Three keys ring together in your pack like a chord. Somewhere above, a plain wooden door is listening.

door_1_elysia.title: The Gatekeeper
door_1_elysia.description:
Elysia's door opens onto a small desk at the foot of the Tower. A ledger. A pen. The old Gatekeeper stands, stretches, and smiles at you for the first time.

'Your turn,' he says, and walks into the light.

You sit. The Tower door creaks open, and a new climber steps inside, bright-eyed and sponsored.

'Name and god,' you hear yourself say.

**TO BE CONTINUED...**

door_2_sepulchure.title: The Warden
door_2_sepulchure.description:
Sepulchure's door opens onto a throne of bones on Floor 4. 'Not a god,' he says. 'Not yet. A warden. You'll keep a floor, take a tithe, and never climb again.'

You sit. The throne fits.

Somewhere below, a climber is on the stairs, and you find that you are hungry.

**TO BE CONTINUED...**

door_3_drakath.title: Every Floor at Once
door_3_drakath.description:
Drakath's door opens onto everything. You are on Floor 1 and Floor 30. You are on your first climb and your last. You are beside Wren on 13, and she is laughing, and she is gone.

'Free of the line!' Drakath cheers. 'Trapped in the circle! The best of both!'

You try to scream. You do it forever, once.

**TO BE CONTINUED...**

door_4_freedom.title: The Fourth Door
door_4_freedom.description:
You walk past the gods. For the first time, they stop smiling.

'That door isn't-'
'-it leads Outside-'
'-we can't follow you there.'

The keys turn. The door opens on wind and real sunlight. Far below, faintly, you hear chalk scratching on stone: Wren, keeping the Tower busy for you.

You step through, and fall.

Beneath you lies Asterra: green valleys, silver rivers, and three armies under three banners. Near a village called Bramblewick, a bell begins to ring as a burning star drops out of a clear sky. Across the land, a shadow shaped like a broken crown turns to look.

The crater is still smoking when they find you.

**TO BE CONTINUED IN: CROWNFALL**

30.title: The Rite
30.description:
The gods step back, glowing brighter than before. Brighter with what they just took from you.

'Well climbed,' says Elysia. Behind them, three doors swing open: one gold, one black, one that won't hold still.

'Choose,' says Sepulchure. 'Everyone chooses.'

variants.description:
The gods step back, glowing brighter than before. Brighter with what they just took from you.

'Well climbed,' says Elysia. Behind them, three doors swing open: one gold, one black, one that won't hold still.

And behind those, where there was only wall, stands a fourth door of plain, weathered wood with three keyholes. The keys in your pack are warm.
